concepts.title: Polygons: Convex and Concave
concepts.definition: A simple closed curve made up of only line segments is called a polygon. Polygons that are convex have no portions of their diagonals in their exteriors; any line segment joining any two different points in the interior of a convex polygon lies wholly in the interior of it. In this class we deal with convex polygons only.
concepts.formula: polygon = simple closed curve made up of only line segments
concepts.key_idea: Polygon: simple, closed, all sides line segments; convex keeps diagonals inside.

concepts.title: Regular and Irregular Polygons
concepts.definition: A regular polygon is both equiangular and equilateral. For example, a square has sides of equal length and angles of equal measure, hence it is a regular polygon. A rectangle is equiangular but not equilateral, so it is not a regular polygon.
concepts.key_idea: Regular means all angles equal AND all sides equal.

concepts.title: Sum of Exterior Angles of a Polygon
concepts.definition: The sum of the measures of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. This is true whatever be the number of sides of the polygon. For a regular polygon all exterior angles are equal, so each exterior angle = 360 / number of sides.
concepts.formula: sum of exterior angles = 360 degrees; each exterior angle of regular polygon = 360 / n
concepts.key_idea: Exterior angles of any polygon add to 360 degrees.

concepts.title: Number of Sides from an Exterior or Interior Angle
concepts.definition: Total measure of all exterior angles of a regular polygon is 360 degrees. If the measure of each exterior angle is known, the number of sides = 360 / measure of each exterior angle. If each interior angle is given, first find the exterior angle = 180 - interior angle (they form a linear pair).
concepts.formula: number of sides = 360 / exterior_angle; exterior_angle = 180 - interior_angle
concepts.key_idea: Divide 360 by the exterior angle to get the number of sides.

concepts.title: Trapezium
concepts.definition: Trapezium is a quadrilateral with a pair of parallel sides. If the non-parallel sides of a trapezium are of equal length, we call it an isosceles trapezium.
concepts.formula: trapezium = quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides
concepts.key_idea: One pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium; equal non-parallel sides make it isosceles.

concepts.title: Kite
concepts.definition: Kite is a special type of a quadrilateral. A kite has 4 sides (it is a quadrilateral) and there are exactly two distinct consecutive pairs of sides of equal length, for example AB = AD and BC = CD.
concepts.formula: kite = quadrilateral with exactly two distinct consecutive pairs of equal sides
concepts.key_idea: Two pairs of equal consecutive sides, but not all four equal.

concepts.title: Parallelogram and its Side Properties
concepts.definition: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral whose opposite sides are parallel. Property: the opposite sides of a parallelogram are of equal length. Elements: AB and DC are opposite sides, AB and BC are adjacent sides (one side starts where the other ends).
concepts.formula: opposite sides parallel and equal; perimeter = 2 x (side1 + side2)
concepts.key_idea: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal.

concepts.title: Angles of a Parallelogram
concepts.definition: Property: the opposite angles of a parallelogram are of equal measure. Property: the adjacent angles in a parallelogram are supplementary (they add to 180 degrees) since they are interior opposite angles on parallel lines.
concepts.formula: opposite angles equal; adjacent angles supplementary: angle + adjacent_angle = 180
concepts.key_idea: Opposite angles equal, adjacent angles add to 180 degrees.

concepts.title: Diagonals of a Parallelogram
concepts.definition: The diagonals of a parallelogram, in general, are not of equal length. Property: the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other (at the point of their intersection). This gives AO = CO and BO = DO.
concepts.key_idea: Diagonals of a parallelogram cut each other into equal halves.

concepts.title: Rhombus
concepts.definition: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with sides of equal length. Since the opposite sides of a rhombus have the same length, it is also a parallelogram; so a rhombus has all the properties of a parallelogram and also that of a kite. Property: the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular bisectors of one another.
concepts.formula: all sides equal; diagonals are perpendicular bisectors of one another
concepts.key_idea: Rhombus: all sides equal; diagonals perpendicular bisectors.

concepts.title: Rectangle
concepts.definition: A rectangle is a parallelogram with equal angles; that is, a parallelogram in which every angle is a right angle (each angle measures 90 degrees because 4x = 360 gives x = 90). Property: the diagonals of a rectangle are of equal length, and besides being equal they bisect each other.
concepts.formula: each angle = 90 degrees; diagonals equal and bisect each other
concepts.key_idea: Rectangle: parallelogram with a right angle; diagonals equal.

concepts.title: Square
concepts.definition: A square is a rectangle with equal sides. This means a square has all the properties of a rectangle with an additional requirement that all the sides have equal length. In a square the diagonals (i) bisect one another (square being a parallelogram), (ii) are of equal length (square being a rectangle) and (iii) are perpendicular to one another. Property: the diagonals of a square are perpendicular bisectors of each other.
concepts.formula: all sides equal, all angles 90; diagonals equal, bisect each other, perpendicular
concepts.key_idea: Square: rectangle with equal sides; diagonals are equal perpendicular bisectors.
